title: Beef Fried Rice with Soft Egg
summary: Takeaway-style beef fried rice. The secret is dry, cold rice, deeply browned beef and soft eggs cooked on their own first.

steps.heading: Cook the rice
steps.text: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear.
Put the rice and the water in a saucepan, bring to the boil, then cover and turn the heat down to its lowest setting.
Cook for {timer:12|rice} without lifting the lid, then turn off the heat and leave it covered for {timer:10|rice rest}.

Spread the rice on a large plate or tray to let the steam out. Ideally, refrigerate it until cold: cold, dry rice fries much better than freshly cooked rice. If you are cooking straight away, let it cool as much as possible while you prepare everything else.

steps.heading: Prepare everything
steps.text: Separate the white parts of the spring onions from the green tops, and slice both thinly.
Mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, Shaoxing wine, white pepper and MSG in a small bowl. Beat the eggs in another bowl.
Keep the garlic, ginger and tomato paste ready beside the hob. Once you start frying, things move quickly.

steps.heading: Cook the eggs
steps.text: Put the empty stainless-steel pan over a medium heat for {timer:1-2}.

Test it with a few drops of water. If they form little beads that glide around the pan, it is ready; if they evaporate at once, it is too hot. Wipe the water away carefully and let the pan dry completely.
Turn the heat down to medium-low and let the pan cool slightly for {timer:20-30s}. Add the olive oil for the eggs and swirl it around the pan.

Add the beaten eggs. They should start to set gently rather than brown straight away. Stir slowly with a spatula until softly scrambled, and lift them onto a plate while they are still slightly moist.

steps.heading: Brown the beef
steps.text: Turn the heat up to medium-high and add a little olive oil if needed. Add the beef mince, spreading it across the pan.
Leave it undisturbed for {timer:1-2} so it browns properly, then break it up and keep cooking until browned and cooked through, {timer:4-6} in all.
If there is a lot of liquid, let it evaporate before you go on. Good browning is what gives the dish its deep, savoury flavour.

steps.heading: Build the flavour
steps.text: Push the beef to one side of the pan, or lift it out for a moment if the pan is crowded.
Add the spring onion whites, the garlic and the ginger, with a little olive oil if needed. Fry for {timer:30-45s}, stirring constantly, without letting the garlic burn.
Add the tomato paste and cook for another {timer:45-60s}, stirring it into the beef. This takes away the raw tomato taste and adds colour. Return the beef to the pan if you lifted it out.

steps.heading: Fry the rice
steps.text: Add the cold rice, breaking up any clumps with the spatula. Spread it out and let it fry for {timer:30-60s} before tossing.
Stir-fry for another {timer:2-3}, until the rice is hot and coated in the beef and tomato.
Pour the sauce around the hot sides of the pan, then toss everything together.
Return the scrambled eggs and break them gently into bite-sized pieces. Add the spring onion greens and toss for {timer:30s} more.
Taste before adding any salt: the oyster sauce and soy sauce are already salty.

steps.heading: Serve
steps.text: Serve straight away while the rice is hot, finished with a few fresh spring onion greens and a small pinch of white pepper.

tips: If the eggs stick at once, the pan is too hot or the oil has not spread properly. Lower the heat and do not try to force them off.
No sugar or sesame oil is needed.
The three things that make it: properly chilled rice, deeply browned beef, and eggs cooked separately so they stay soft rather than dry and rubbery.
